# Datatype contract (raw SQL type → canonical semantic type → model-matrix type)

Types are declared, never inferred: `falls_ml.data.meuhedet_wide.coerce_wide_types` casts every column to the declared pandas dtype and reports each value that does not fit (`wrong_type`, with the offending values for date columns); the build stops on any wrong-type value in a column it uses. Date text is read only with the source layouts the contract declares (`contract.date_formats`, in trial order), so 01/02/2024 has exactly one meaning; the loader refuses a set in which two formats would read the same text differently (no day/month inference), and anything no declared format fits is a counted wrong-type value, never a guess or an Excel serial number. Dates land in `datetime64[us]`, which holds the whole SQL date range; only the canonical modelling dates (index_date, predictor_max_record_date, outcome_first_event_date, death_date, followup_end_date) are cast to `datetime64[ns]`, and a value that range cannot hold is never converted silently. `NULL` is never converted to 0 unless the mapping manifest declares the eFalls `absent_is_zero` rule for that predictor, and every such conversion is counted in the build report.

## Semantic types

| semantic_type | pandas_dtype | model_dtype | rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| identifier | string | never | never enters a model matrix; never printed by the audit |
| date | datetime64[us] (contract layer, full SQL date range 0001..9999) → datetime64[ns] for the canonical modelling dates only | never | raw dates never enter a model; derived Days_Since_* columns do; used for the D-00 timing check; far-future business sentinels (e.g. 2999-12-31 = open-ended SCD row) stay dates and must be declared per column (sentinels / sentinel_means / sentinel_modeling_rule); an undeclared far-future date in a column the build uses stops the build naming column, value and expected type |
| binary | Int64 (nullable) | int8_binary | allowed {0,1}; NULL keeps its business meaning (not assessed / source absent); 0 only by a declared eFalls absent_is_zero rule |
| count | Int64 (nullable) | float64 | non-negative integers; NULL = source absent / not applicable (declared per column) |
| continuous | float64 / Int64 | float64 | numeric; NULL = not measured (missing indicator + training-derived imputation in Phase 2) |
| categorical | Int64 or string | onehot_categorical | codes are labels, never magnitudes; one-hot encoded; NULL = missing category when declared |
| ordinal | Int64 / float64 | ordinal_float64 | ordered score with a declared range; NULL = not assessed (missing category) |
| quality_control | Int64 / string | never | QA / control field; audited, never a predictor |
| label | Int64 / string | never | outcome and outcome-support columns; never a predictor |

## SQL → pandas

| sql | pandas |
|---|---|
| int | Int64 |
| smallint | Int64 |
| tinyint | Int64 |
| bit | Int64 |
| decimal | float64 |
| date | datetime64[us] |
| datetime | datetime64[us] |
| varchar | string |

## Declared source date formats (text cells; trial order)

| order | strptime_format | example | reads_as |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | %Y-%m-%d | 2024-02-01 | 2024-02-01 |
| 2 | %d/%m/%Y | 01/02/2024 | 2024-02-01 |

Real Excel and Parquet date cells are taken as they are. The audit reports which format read each column (`datatype_audit.source_date_formats`).
